lateral_flank_blob_constellation.centroid_triangulation: High-luminance circular pixel clusters are arranged in approximately vertical columns posterior to the gill slits. The clusters are most distinct and largest in the mid-flank region, decreasing in diameter and intensity towards the caudal peduncle.
lateral_flank_blob_constellation.stripe_intersections: Vertical bands of elevated pixel intensity are clearly visible, intersecting with the circular blobs to form a regular grid-like pattern of anchor nodes across the central lateral surface.

carinae_gradient_vectors.ridge_trajectory: Three prominent horizontal ridges are visible on the upper flank, characterized by a sharp vertical intensity gradient with specular highlights on the dorsal-facing edges and shadow casting on the ventral-facing edges.

dorsal_fin_surface_patterning.internal_spot_density: The first dorsal fin silhouette contains a sparse distribution of small, high-luminance spots, primarily visible along the lower half and leading edge, though partially obscured by surface light refraction.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A distinct irregular notch is visible on the posterior trailing edge of the left pectoral fin. Several remoras are attached to the ventral surface and near the base of the caudal fin.
other_distinctive_markers: The entire visible dorsal and lateral surface is covered by a high-contrast caustic network caused by surface wave light refraction, which creates moving, high-intensity linear artifacts over the shark's skin.
